title: org-sync-spotlight-bottleneck-breakouts-jul-07-2026
content:
Quick note: this is the writeup from the org sync on 2026-07-07 (weekly engineering sync + focused breakout on latency bottlenecks). Meeting was recorded; highlights and action items below.

Attendees: eng leadership, platform eng squads, runtime, infra, SRE, product-hosted-api, solutions-eng. See collaborators for smaller breakout leads. Approx 55 people joined live.

Agenda (timeboxed):
- 10m: opening + metrics snapshot (Aisha)
- 20m: incident recap + heatmap spotlight (Marco)
- 25m: 3 parallel breakouts (runtime perf, KV cache strategy, autoscaler tuning)
- 15m: rollouts & product notes (Priya)
- 10m: Q&A + close

1) Opening / high-level metrics (2 mins)
- Weekly KPIs: median p95 latency for text generate route 120ms -> 140ms (regression after Tuesday deploy).
- Error rate: overall 0.18% (up from 0.07% last week), spike correlated with model swap event on 2026-07-06.
- Dedicated utilization: 78% average across pools; burst cushion at ~18%.
- Cost per 1k tokens increased by ~6% week-over-week due to hot-path tail latency causing more queued requests.

2) Incident recap + heatmap spotlight (10 mins)
- Summary: quick degradation on 2026-07-06 03:40 UTC impacting text-generation for 18 minutes. Root cause preliminary: under-estimated KV cache memory pressure when new longer-context model variant (gptx-extended) hit production. Cache eviction policy didn't evict aggressively; memory thrashing caused GC stalls on worker processes.
- Impact: elevated latencies and a small percent of dropped streams for 18 minutes. No data leakage.
- Detection: SRE alert threshold triggered by queue growth + p99 spike; automatic fallback to smaller model version didn't activate due to a routing policy mismatch (policy targeted by model id not by family).
- Heatmap: Marco walked through the infra heatmap (linked) showing correlated CPU steal on nodes hosting the new variant.
- Immediate mitigations performed: temporarily pinned traffic away from gptx-extended, increased cache eviction aggressiveness, bounced 6 nodes for clean memory states.

Decision: Add model-family routing in smart-routing policies to ensure fallbacks work for family-level incompatibilities. Owner: Marco. Due: 2026-07-14. (JIRA: JIRA-INF-4321)

3) Breakouts summary (each breakout lead provided 5-min recap)
A) Serving runtime perf (lead: Elena)
- Focus: sequence length path optimization and attention kernel selection.
- Findings: the new variant uses longer prompt prefixes causing kernel fallback to slower path. In tests, switching to an alternate fused attention kernel reduces p95 by ~22% for sequences >2048 tokens.
- Action: prototype a selective kernel switcher based on incoming request histogram. Prototype PR: github PR 981. Owner: Elena. Due: 2026-07-21 for staging test.
- Risk: need to validate across A100 and H100 instants; some kernels regress on V1 microcode.

B) KV cache & memory policy (lead: Jonah)
- Focus: eviction heuristics, prefix caching, and cross-request sharing for identical prefixes.
- Findings: 28% of requests share top-5 prefixes across the last 24h (chat assistants), opportunity for prefix dedupe.
- Short-term: tighten eviction to LRU with size buckets (small, medium, large entries) to avoid single huge conversation monopolizing memory. Owner: Jonah. Due: 2026-07-12.
- Mid-term: evaluate dedupe layer that stores symbolically-referenced prefix blocks (design doc to be drafted). Owner: Jonah + runtime architects. Due: 2026-08-02.

C) Autoscaler & routing (lead: Priya)
- Focus: scale-up latency and routing fallback policies.
- Findings: scale-up cool-down currently 90s — for bursty workloads this causes queuing. We can safely reduce to 45s for pools with headroom in reserved capacity. Also found routing mismatch that prevented family-level fallback (see Incident above).
- Action: change cool-down to 45s for pools tagged 'burst-ready', implement routing family-key. Owners: Priya (autoscaler change), Marco (routing). Due: 2026-07-14.

4) Rollouts & product notes (Priya)
- Private deployments: onboarding checklist updated; first private pilot slated for mid-Aug. Need infra readiness checklist completed by infra team (networking + KMS).
- Dedicated: upcoming commit Q3 requires updating SLO docs; product asked for clearer per-tenant throughput guidance (doc link in artifacts).
- Hosted API: product request to add route-level token budget per-request for customers to reduce accidental runaway generations. Priya to scope.

5) Engineering org housekeeping
- Hiring: platform-eng made 3 offers; expect two starts in Aug. Still hiring 2x runtime engineers and 1x infra reliability.
- Oncall rotations: new rotation published; reminder to update runbooks after any incident.
- Training: sync with SRE for kernel-ops workshop on 2026-07-23 (hands-on tracing). RSVP requested.

6) Action items (short list, owners, dates)
- JIRA-INF-4321: Add family-level routing fallback + unit tests — Owner: Marco — Due: 2026-07-14.
- PR-981 stabilization: finish benchmarks on H100 & A100, add microcode guard rails — Owner: Elena — Due: 2026-07-21.
- KV eviction rollout: implement size-bucket LRU + monitor — Owner: Jonah — Due: 2026-07-12.
- Autoscaler cool-down change for 'burst-ready' pools — Owner: Priya — Due: 2026-07-14.
- Draft prefix-dedupe design doc — Owners: Jonah, runtime-architects — Due: 2026-08-02.
- Runbook updates after incident (postmortem draft) — Owner: Marco + SRE — Due: 2026-07-09 (postmortem to be attached).

7) Open questions / flagged work
- How aggressively do we allow kernel selection to vary per-request? (perf testing needed)
- Should Dedicated customers get an option to pin kernel families for determinism? Product to weigh in.
- Cost impact estimate for prefix dedupe (storage vs compute trade-off). Finance to model.

8) Decisions made in meeting
- Reduce autoscaler cool-down to 45s for flagged pools.
- Prioritize family-level routing changes as critical for safe rollouts.
- Kick off prefix-dedupe design as medium priority.

9) Notes to follow-up channels
- Slack thread: #eng-runtime "org-sync 07-07 followups" (pinned).
- Confluence: updated heatmap + incident timeline attached (link in artifacts).
- Expect a short postmortem draft by 2026-07-09; will move to final after 48h review.

Quick loose notes / scribbles captured during meeting (raw):
- "kernel fallback path is a liability if we keep swapping model variants frequently"
- "we need synthetic load tests that mimic chat prefix reuse"
- "make the autoscaler policy pluggable by pool class"

If you own an action item and need more time, call it out on the ticket and tag me.

Next sync: 2026-07-14 (regular weekly), planned focus: Dedicated capacity economics + rollout checklist for private pilot.

— Aisha
